title: Pluggable subpage priority scheduler and OOM grace plan for paged KV
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background:
The current paged/blocked KV cache uses coarse slab pages (1–4MB) and a single LRU pass for eviction. As continuous batching and token-locality patterns diversified, we observed pathological OOMs when a few long-context requests pinned many large pages and batch density increased. Existing tickets (see ENG-613579 and ENG-91234) explored residency prioritization and lazy materialization, but lacked a unified scheduler with an OOM grace strategy for bursty workloads.

Goals:
- Introduce a pluggable subpage-priority scheduler that operates at 64KB–256KB subpage granularity inside larger page slabs.
- Provide an OOM grace/recovery plan that degrades gracefully (spill, degrade quantization, fall back to host cache) instead of hard OOMs.
- Keep per-request latency SLOs for common tails while reducing mean token cost.
- Maintain observability hooks for hotspot tracing and postmortem for any eviction/oom events.

Proposal (high-level):
1) Subpage layout and metadata:
   - Page slab stays as allocation unit for GPU buffer objects (e.g., 4MB), but the runtime tracks subpages of 128KB (configurable).
   - Each subpage has metadata: last_access_ts, hotness_score (decay window), tenant_id, request_affinity_token (hashed prefix of prompt), pinned_flag, and origin_hint (model, quantized/float).
   - Metadata stored in host-side compact table (one cache-line per subpage) and mirrored lightly on device for fast checks during token loop.

2) Pluggable priority scheduler API:
   - Scheduler interface: score(subpage, incoming_batch_context) -> integer priority.
   - Default implementation: hybrid score = (LRU_age_weight * age_rank) + (affinity_weight * token_affinity_score) + (batch_density_weight * batch_locality_score) - (pinned_penalty).
   - We will ship two builtin schedulers: "hotset-first" (favor hot subpages) and "fair-tenant" (ensure tenant budgets). Teams can register custom schedulers via a C++ plugin or remote-config snippet.

3) Prefetching and admission control:
   - For a batch, scheduler scores needed subpages and requests async DMA prefetch for top-K by score, subject to a concurrent-prefetch budget.
   - If the sum of sizes for top-K exceeds safe-residency threshold, admission control rejects low-priority requests or routes them to a lower-cost model variant (quantized / CPU fallback) per routing policy.

4) OOM grace / recovery policy:
   - Soft OOM signal: when available GPU free memory dips below a configurable watermark, emit soft_oom event rather than immediate OOM.
   - Grace actions (attempted in order):
       a) Evict cold subpages synchronously using scheduler (prefer subpages without active KV references).
       b) Trigger immediate on-the-fly model quantization fallback for the requesting model variant (if available).
       c) Spill lowest-priority subpages to pinned host staging buffers (persisted in paged host slab) and update page table to mark as host-resident.
       d) If none succeed, run admission control to shed or queue low-priority requests with a configurable backoff.
   - If a hard OOM still occurs, capture full eviction trace, heap snapshots, and a deterministic replay token that can reproduce memory pressure for postmortem.

5) Integration with continuous batching and KV cache lifetime:
   - The scheduler consumes batch context: predicted sequence-length, request affinity hashes, and kernel memory hints.
   - KV entries touched within the same batch get a transient boost to hotness (batch-locality credit) which decays quickly.
   - Keep KV lease semantics: long-running streams (chat) may pin a subpage with a short lease; leases expire and can be renewed. Excessive renewals count against tenant residency budgets.

6) Observability and metrics:
   - New metrics: subpage_hotness_histogram, soft_oom_events_by_tenant, prefetch_hit_rate, spill_to_host_count, host-residency_latency_p50/p95, scheduler_decision_latency.
   - Traces: annotate span with "scheduler_decision" and include top-3 scored subpages for each batch.
   - Dashboards: per-model and per-tenant OOM heatmaps and a timeline of eviction/prefetch actions.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Granularity: smaller subpages reduce unnecessary eviction but increase metadata overhead. We chose 128KB default as a balance; can be tuned per workload.
- Host-mirroring metadata vs device-only: storing compact metadata on host keeps GPU memory minimal but adds an extra hop for checks. To keep latency low, we mirror hot-subset indices on device for fast path.
- Scheduler complexity vs determinism: pluggable schedulers allow experiments but require sandboxing; plugins run in the runtime process with a restricted sandbox and time budget.

Progress and engineering notes:
- Prototype (prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-paging/PR-458) implemented subpage metadata and the hotset-first scheduler with prefetch stubs.
- Microbenchmarks: 5–12% tail latency improvement for multi-tenant small-batch workloads and 18% reduction in spill IOPS on headroom tests. Data: drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/kv-paging-v2-benchmarks (internal).
- Early integration tests failing in edge-case with pinned leases and long context streams causing eviction thrashing. Root cause: lease renewal policy allowed indefinite pinning; temporary mitigation added "renewal_count" cap per lease.

Open work (next steps):
- Finalize plugin API and implement sandboxing/timeout for scheduler callbacks (owner: Arjun, 2 wks).
- Implement host spill path with async restore logic and GC of host staging buffer (owner: Lina Gomez, 3 wks).
- Add admission-control routes and model-variant routing integration (owner: Priya Desai, 2 wks).
- Harden metrics and add per-tenant budget enforcement (owner: SRE team, collaboration).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for scheduler determinism in synthetic workloads (coverage target 95%).
- Canary rollout on dedicated capacity only (low-risk) for 2 weeks with soft-oom alerts enabled.
- Migrate to hosted API after telemetry confirms <0.5 soft_ooms/day per cluster and no customer-visible hard OOMs for 7 days.

Acceptance criteria (DONE):
- Scheduler API implemented and hotset-first + fair-tenant schedulers exist and can be selected via config.
- Soft_oom path executes the full grace actions without causing hard OOMs on testbeds under 2x production pressure.
- Observability surfaces for subpage metrics, scatter traces, and per-tenant accounting are present.
- Confluence design doc linked and reviewed (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Paged+Subpage+Scheduler).
